sources.title: WID Methodology
sources.why_it_matters: Measurement anchor for income and wealth distribution data.

sources.title: Regional Wealth Inequality / Global Economic Inequality
sources.why_it_matters: Current benchmark for regional private/public wealth, top shares, bottom shares, and labor share trends.

sources.title: Income and wealth inequalities: Society at a Glance 2024
sources.why_it_matters: Compact OECD benchmark for wealth concentration and cross-country comparison.

sources.title: How to Tax Wealth
sources.why_it_matters: Current guide to the tradeoffs between capital income taxes, wealth taxes, and inheritance taxes.

sources.title: Inheritance Taxation in OECD Countries
sources.why_it_matters: Best compact source in this archive on inheritance-tax equity, efficiency, design, and the warning that wealth may stay concentrated among older cohorts for longer while inheritance age rises.

sources.title: Taxation and Inequality
sources.why_it_matters: Recent overview of how tax systems can mitigate or worsen inequality.

sources.title: Affordable housing: Society at a Glance 2024
sources.why_it_matters: Shows how housing cost burdens intensify inequality and why social housing matters.

sources.title: The Role of Firms in Wage Inequality
sources.why_it_matters: Links employer concentration, bargaining power, and wage inequality.

sources.title: Collective bargaining and social dialogue
sources.why_it_matters: Concise anchor for why bargaining institutions still matter.

sources.title: Competition and market dynamism
sources.why_it_matters: Shows concentration and markups as inequality-relevant market structure issues.

sources.title: G20 background note on the impact of growth on inequality
sources.why_it_matters: Useful current synthesis on redistribution, education spending, labor institutions, and inequality dynamics.

sources.title: Modeling the Impact of a Federal Baby Bonds Program
sources.why_it_matters: Operational evidence point for social inheritance / baby-bond design.

sources.title: Mapping trends and gaps in household wealth across OECD countries
sources.why_it_matters: Recent OECD synthesis on mixed post-2010 wealth trends, housing entry barriers, and demographic wealth gaps.

sources.title: Membership of unions and employers' organisations, and bargaining coverage
sources.why_it_matters: Current OECD evidence on long-run erosion of union density and collective bargaining coverage.

sources.title: Anti-Corruption and Integrity Outlook 2024 — overview
sources.why_it_matters: Anchor for lobbying, political-finance, and integrity-framework weaknesses relevant to wealth-to-rule conversion.

sources.title: Distribution of household wealth in line with national accounts
sources.why_it_matters: Key new anchor for wealth composition: bottom quintile often negative wealth, inequality driven by financial assets, and housing as the largest household asset.

sources.title: Economic insecurity in Europe and potential policy responses
sources.why_it_matters: Compact anchor for liquid-asset resilience and household shock buffers; highlights widespread financial fragility and the policy need to build buffers against income shocks.

sources.title: Building pathways to opportunity
sources.why_it_matters: Compact 2025 opportunity anchor: over 25% of market-income inequality is tied to inherited circumstances across the OECD, parental background contributes over 60% of inequality of opportunity in most countries, and the policy mix includes child development accounts, inheritance taxation, and social housing.

sources.title: Informing policy: What can be done to ensure a more level playing field?
sources.why_it_matters: Compact 2025 anchor for the intergenerational persistence of homeownership, the larger wealth premium from earlier-life transfers, and the case for anti-dynasty housing and inheritance policy.

sources.title: Reigniting investment for more resilient growth
sources.why_it_matters: Narrow new anchor for rising concentration, higher markups, superstar-firm investment concentration, and common-ownership pressures that can rapidly reconcentrate wealth after reform.

sources.title: Financial hardship and out-of-pocket expenditure
sources.why_it_matters: Compact anchor for why healthcare financial protection changes how much precautionary private wealth households need; shows that weak protection can deepen poverty and inequality.

sources.title: Pensions at a Glance 2025
sources.why_it_matters: Compact anchor for why pension design and first-tier benefits change how much private wealth households must hold to avoid old-age insecurity and inequality.

sources.title: Beneficial Ownership and Tax Transparency – Implementation and Remaining Challenges
sources.org: OECD / Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes
sources.why_it_matters: Compact anchor for visible-wealth state capacity: beneficial ownership transparency, implementation gaps, and the institutional preconditions for tracing major fortunes, transfers, and control rights.

sources.title: Household debt
sources.why_it_matters: Compact measurement anchor for household liabilities, especially mortgages and consumer credit, as a share of disposable income.

sources.title: Household financial fragility and asset poverty in OECD regions
sources.why_it_matters: New 2025 anchor for why net-wealth snapshots should be read together with asset poverty and financial fragility rather than assumed to equal resilience.

sources.title: Institutional Investor Engagement and Stewardship
sources.why_it_matters: Current OECD anchor for institutional-ownership concentration, asset-manager dominance in listed equity, information asymmetries between asset owners and managers, and tools such as pass-through voting.

sources.title: To Have and Have Not – How to bridge the gap in opportunities
sources.why_it_matters: Compact 2025 anchor for why household-level inequality measures can understate person-level inequality; notes that gender effects become much stronger when measured using individual earnings rather than household market income.

sources.title: Assets — Gender Data Portal
sources.why_it_matters: Compact World Bank anchor that women often trail men in account and land ownership and that asset access matters for shock resilience and poverty escape.

sources.title: Increasing Women's Ownership and Control of Productive Assets
sources.why_it_matters: Compact World Bank anchor for why household membership alone does not guarantee participation in the benefits of property when formal or enforceable individual rights are weak.

sources.title: Gender pension gap: Pensions at a Glance 2025
sources.why_it_matters: Compact OECD anchor for why household disposable-income gaps can hide much larger person-level pension gaps in old age.

sources.title: Addressing Inequality in Budgeting
sources.why_it_matters: Compact operating anchor for integrating distributional impact analysis into the budget process, using linked administrative data, microsimulation, transparency, and ex ante plus ex post evaluation.

sources.title: Exceptional Public Solvency Support to the Banking Sector: Pitfalls and Good Practices
sources.why_it_matters: Compact 2025 IMF anchor for treating public solvency support as a last resort, maximising burden sharing, minimising moral hazard, protecting taxpayers, and recovering support costs where possible.

sources.title: Addressing Market Dysfunction and Liquidity Stresses in Nonbank Financial Intermediaries
sources.why_it_matters: Compact 2025 IMF anchor for why broad asset purchases can create moral hazard by backstopping asset holders, and why more targeted, collateralised support better limits risk transfer.

sources.title: Global Compendium of Land Value Capture Policies
sources.org: OECD / Lincoln Institute of Land Policy / PKU-Lincoln Institute Center
sources.why_it_matters: Core anchor for the principle that governments can capture land-value uplifts generated by public interventions such as infrastructure investment or land-use changes.

sources.title: Strengthening policies and institutions to increase housing affordability and investment in Czechia
sources.why_it_matters: Recent concrete anchor for basing affordable-housing requirements on increases in land value from development approvals and managing public land strategically to recover value created by public investment or zoning changes.

sources.title: Housing Taxation in OECD Countries
sources.why_it_matters: Broad anchor for the claim that mortgage-interest relief and uncapped main-residence capital-gains exemptions can be regressive, distort saving choices, and raise house prices rather than widen entry.

sources.title: Financial Incentives and Retirement Savings
sources.why_it_matters: Core design anchor for retirement-saving support; shows tax incentives mainly move middle-to-high income earners while low-income earners respond better to matching contributions and fixed nominal subsidies.

sources.title: International community meets in New Delhi to reflect on latest advances in global tax transparency
sources.org: OECD / Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes
sources.why_it_matters: Current 2025 anchor that cross-border tax transparency is already operating at scale: automatic exchange now covers 116 jurisdictions, 171 million accounts and nearly EUR 13 trillion in assets, with substantial revenue gains already identified.

sources.title: Comparative Assessment of Asset Requirements for Minimum Income Benefit Recipients
sources.why_it_matters: Compact 2025 OECD anchor for why asset tests in minimum-income schemes are widespread, highly diverse, often complex, and relevant to benefit adequacy, coverage, take-up, and long-term self-sufficiency rather than being a mere technical afterthought.

sources.title: Modernising Access to Social Protection
sources.why_it_matters: Current OECD anchor for why non-take-up, information complexity, hassle costs, renewal burden, and digital exclusion weaken the real social floor, and for why linked data, pre-filled claims, automatic enrolment, live support, and multiple channels matter for claimability.

sources.title: Protection Gaps in Retirement Savings
sources.why_it_matters: Current OECD anchor for why long vesting periods, weak portability across schemes, and employer- or sector-tied entitlements can strand mobile workers and make long-run asset claims less durable than headline enrolment suggests.

sources.title: HC1.2 Housing Costs over Income
sources.why_it_matters: Narrow OECD anchor that total housing costs include structural insurance, mandatory services and charges, regular maintenance and repair, taxes, and utilities, and that these costs can materially raise burdens even for owners.

sources.title: HC2.1 Living Space
sources.why_it_matters: Narrow OECD anchor that housing adequacy depends on household composition, that overcrowding adjusts for household members' age, gender, and relationship rather than room count alone, and that overcrowding is higher in low-income households in many countries.

sources.title: Land 2030 – About
sources.why_it_matters: Current World Bank anchor that land and property-rights reform contributes to growth, urbanisation, domestic resource mobilisation, job creation, gender equality, conflict mitigation, and social cohesion, while many people still lack secure land rights and insecurity is worse for women and Indigenous Peoples.

sources.title: Consumer Finance Risk Monitor 2026
sources.why_it_matters: Current OECD anchor that low financial literacy remains a top consumer-side risk, that only a minority of adults reach the OECD/INFE minimum target score, and that ordinary people often do not seek independent advice when choosing financial products, which supports the archive's anti-maze / low-expertise-operability rule.

sources.title: Annual survey of financial incentives for retirement savings
sources.why_it_matters: Current OECD country-profile anchor on retirement-saving incentive design, with rules applicable as of July 2025, useful for checking whether asset-building support is delivered through flatter non-tax incentives or through designs that scale more strongly with prior tax liability and contribution size.

sources.title: Intergenerational social mobility across OECD countries
sources.why_it_matters: Current 2026 OECD cross-country anchor that parental background still strongly shapes earnings, women's labour market participation, and educational outcomes in most countries, and that equalising opportunity often requires more than formal schooling parity because family background can continue to influence adult outcomes even among similarly educated people.

sources.title: Geographic inequalities in access to opportunities
sources.why_it_matters: Current 2025 OECD anchor that opportunities in education, employment, services, and infrastructure vary significantly within countries by place; metropolitan and higher-income regions and neighbourhoods tend to offer better access and mobility; smaller geographic units reveal disparities hidden by larger averages; and many people cannot simply move to better places because mobility has real financial and care costs.

sources.title: Competition challenges in prudential regulation
sources.why_it_matters: Current 2025 OECD anchor that state support and expectations of public support can entrench incumbent advantages, lower their funding costs, weaken entry or expansion by rivals, and raise TBTF and competition concerns rather than operating as distributionally neutral stabilisation.

sources.title: Personal Insolvency and Data Collection Systems
sources.why_it_matters: Current 2025 IMF anchor that personal insolvency systems can reduce duplicated enforcement and fire-sale losses, provide a real second chance, help prevent homelessness, reduce welfare reliance, force creditor realism about low-value claims, and encourage more careful lending through fairer burden sharing and better lender risk internalisation.

sources.title: Household financial fragility and asset poverty in OECD regions
sources.why_it_matters: Current 2025 OECD regional anchor that financial fragility and asset poverty vary widely within countries, that many economic shocks are geographically localised, and that a useful ordinary-stress test is whether households hold enough financial assets or net wealth to cover three months of income at the national poverty-line level.

sources.title: Setting the scene: Demographic change, economic growth and intergenerational inequalities
sources.why_it_matters: Current 2025 OECD anchor that younger cohorts face weaker homeownership in many countries, that lower-income young people have been hit especially hard, and that inheritances are increasingly expected to arrive later in life, often too late to support first housing access or independent early adulthood.

sources.title: Towards a more accessible and sustainable housing market
sources.why_it_matters: Current 2025 OECD housing-policy anchor that further efforts are needed to discourage land speculation, that land-value-capture tools can help recover gains generated by public investment or land-use decisions, and that stronger local incentives and better stock use matter for affordability and build-through.

sources.title: Taking Stock of Progress on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes
sources.org: OECD / Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes
sources.why_it_matters: Current 2025 OECD / Global Forum anchor that, as of 1 July 2025, nearly half of reviewed jurisdictions had not yet reached a satisfactory level of implementation on ownership information, with beneficial-ownership weaknesses and weak practical supervision / enforcement still among the main remaining gaps.

distribution_and_wealth_structure.why: Broad wealth shares, top-tail concentration, household wealth structure, and public/private balance.

tax_inheritance_and_public_revenue.why: Wealth taxation, inheritance taxation, tax incidence, distributional budgeting, and fiscal counterweight design.

housing_land_and_spatial_closure.why: Housing-cost washout, land-value capture, affordability, space, and place-based closure dynamics.

labor_firms_and_market_power.why: Bargaining power, firm effects, competition, markups, and wage-distribution pressures from below.

floor_fragility_and_social_protection.why: Household fragility, debt stress, asset poverty, healthcare and pension security, minimum-income asset tests, claiming, and ordinary-life financial resilience.

intergenerational_opportunity_and_person.why: Social inheritance, unequal starts, gendered ownership, mobility, and person-level foothold formation across the life course.

visibility_stewardship_and_political_fir.why: Beneficial ownership visibility, stewardship concentration, anti-corruption integrity, and anti-capture state capacity.

implementation_budgeting_and_crisis_gove.why: State capacity, budget design, rescue design, liquidity backstops, enforcement infrastructure, and implementation rails.
